nodes.label: Wave-Based Shipping
nodes.rationale: Wave-based shipping: Each wave is end-to-end demoable before the next begins. Acceptance criteria are executable - every task has runnable tests in contracts/.

nodes.norm_label: wave-43: evals harness as first-class directory

nodes.label: API Versioning Header Strategy
nodes.rationale: X-API-Version header on /api/* responses (not URL prefix). OpenAPI version = package version. Additive-only within major. First breaking change ships as /api/v2 URLs; v1 gets 6-month sunset via Deprecation + Sunset headers. Chosen over URL-prefixing for single-tenant internal tool with one SPA consumer.

nodes.label: Client Names APEX INNER INSUDESIGN
nodes.rationale: APEX and INNER are client names, not agreement types. INSUDESIGN is the service name (product), not a client. This was a key correction from early misreading where these were treated as agreement types.

nodes.label: Compliance Standards NBC ECBC IGBC IS
nodes.norm_label: compliance standards nbc ecbc igbc is
nodes.rationale: Building code standards (NBC, ECBC, IGBC, IS fire codes) are stored as reference data per project. These are seeded reference rows, not enums.

nodes.label: Core Business Chain Flow
nodes.rationale: The client's actual MVP: Inquiry → Client → Service Agreement → Token → Document Reference → Time Log → Invoice. This is the heart of the system that directly maps to how staff currently work in Excel sheets.

nodes.label: Docker Compose Stack Components
nodes.rationale: Services: PostgreSQL (database), Redis (cache/queue), MinIO (file storage), backend (FastAPI), worker (Celery), frontend (React/Vite), migrate (Alembic one-shot), adminer (dev-only DB UI). All run as Docker containers.

nodes.label: Excel to ERP Migration Tool
nodes.rationale: One-time migration tool (scripts/import_excel.py) for existing Excel sheets. Supports: inquiries, clients, agreements, tokens, document_references, projects, time_logs, sustainability. Always dry-run first, then commit. Owner for real migration at go-live is organizational decision (Viraj decides).

nodes.label: GST Invoicing Implementation
nodes.rationale: GST implemented at invoice level as of wave-18. Invoice carries gst_percent + gst_amount (Numeric(18,2)), computed as subtotal × gst_percent / 100. Default 18% GST.

nodes.label: Idempotency Keys Implementation
nodes.rationale: Idempotency-Key header on invoice create/generate-from-time/status change. Stored in Postgres idempotency_keys table (not Redis) to survive Redis flush. TTL 24h enforced lazily. Same key + same body = replayed response; same key + different body = 422 error.

nodes.label: Load Testing Results 10-150 Users
nodes.rationale: Load-tested at 10, 50, 100, and 150 concurrent users on dev machine using Locust. Results: p95 ≈ 29-130 ms, no server 5xx errors at any level. Degradation knee between 100 and 150 users. NOT tested on client's Windows Server - that remains unverified.

nodes.label: No Leads Module Decision
nodes.rationale: Per Viraj's instruction, there is no Leads sheet. Lead ID / LDI columns removed entirely - not stored even historically. New work is Inquiry only (SWA-{year}-INQ-...). Migration 0030 drops residual DB column.

nodes.label: Out of MVP Scope Items
nodes.rationale: Explicitly out of MVP per client decisions: HR/Payroll, CRM/Lead Gen, Full Accounting/GL, Mobile App, Real-time Collaboration, AI/ML Features, Multi-tenant SaaS, Advanced BI/OLAP, Webhooks/Public API, SSO/SAML/OIDC, Custom Workflow Engine, Document OCR/Parsing, Resource Scheduling/Gantt, Vendor Portal, Client Portal.

nodes.label: RBAC Role Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Five roles: Admin (everything including user management and finance), PM (inquiries, clients, projects, agreements, tokens, time), Designer (document references, time logging), Auditor (compliance checklists and certify documents, read-only elsewhere), Viewer (read-only browse). Mirrors Excel sheet permissions.

nodes.label: SWA Reference ID Format
nodes.rationale: Every entity uses SWA-{year}-{3-letter-code}-{seq:03d} format (e.g., SWA-2025-INQ-001, SWA-2025-SA-011). Counters reset every calendar year. This matches the live Excel sheets and was confirmed by Viraj.

nodes.label: Soft Delete Policy and Exceptions
nodes.rationale: Soft-delete (deleted_at column) on 20 model files. Intentional exceptions: AuditLog (immutable), ComplianceStandard/ChecklistItem (reference data), ProjectComplianceItem (certification evidence), ExportJob (ownership record), Notification (current UX is mark-read), ReferenceCounter (system sequencing), RefreshToken (uses revoked_at instead), TaskDependency (relationship table). Document deactivates via is_active instead.

nodes.label: SWA ERP Product v1.0.1
nodes.rationale: Internal ERP for SWA Consultancy replacing ~20 Excel files on OneDrive with one web-based system while keeping the same business logic staff already use.

nodes.label: Windows Server Deployment Target
nodes.rationale: Deployment target is Windows Server on-prem with VPN access, 128 GB RAM, expected 100+ concurrent users. Uses Docker Engine (free) + WSL2 + Docker Compose. No IT department scenario documented.

nodes.label: Yearly ID Sequence Reset
nodes.rationale: Reference counters reset every calendar year (e.g., SWA-2025-SA-011 in 2025 becomes SWA-2026-SA-001 in 2026). Confirmed by Viraj. Implemented via reference_counters table keyed by (entity_type, year).

nodes.label: Tech Stack Selection Rationale
nodes.rationale: Backend: Python 3.11 + FastAPI (continuity with Python skills, modern, type-safe, OpenAPI auto-generated, Pydantic v2, async-ready). Database: PostgreSQL 16 (ACID, relational, JSONB, mature). ORM: SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic (declarative, type-safe, migrations). Frontend: React 18 + Vite + TypeScript strict (most-used, fast dev, type-safe). UI: shadcn/ui + Tailwind (composable, own code, utility-first). Server state: TanStack Query (standard React server state). Auth: JWT + bcrypt (stateless, standard). Background jobs: Celery + Redis (standard Python, implemented wave-31). Deploy: Docker Compose first (one-server sufficient, simpler than k8s).

nodes.label: Orchestrator-Workers Pattern
nodes.rationale: Two-tier development: Orchestrator plans + reviews; OpenCode workers execute. Implementation goes to OpenCode CLI workers, orchestrator writes task files into work/<wave>/, reviews reports in work/reports/<wave>/, and merges approved output.

nodes.label: Project Lifecycle States
nodes.rationale: Project lifecycle: Lead → Quote → Awarded → Design → Vendor → Execution → Validation → Closed. Skipping a state requires admin override + ADR.

nodes.rationale: BOQ ingestion is schema-first. Validate before any DB write. Reject with clear errors. No partial inserts.

nodes.rationale: Compliance standards are versioned. NBC 2016, NBC 2024 — code never assumes 'latest'. Standards are data, not code.

nodes.label: Short-Lived JWT Tokens
nodes.rationale: JWT short-lived (1h access, 30d refresh). Rotate refresh tokens.

nodes.label: Money as Decimal(18,2)
nodes.rationale: Money is Decimal(18,2). Never float. INR is the default currency; multi-currency ready.

nodes.label: No Coupling to rfq2boq
nodes.rationale: No coupling to rfq2boq (Project 1). ERP accepts BOQ files of any source. Zero direct API calls between the two products.

nodes.label: Optimistic Locking via Version Column
nodes.rationale: Optimistic locking via version column. Updates require If-Match on critical entities.

nodes.label: Parameterized SQL Queries Only
nodes.rationale: SQL via parameterized queries only. No string concatenation, no f-strings into SQL.

nodes.label: Performance Budgets
nodes.rationale: Performance budgets. API <500ms P95, page load <1.5s P95, BOQ parse <30s for 100 lines.

nodes.label: Server-Side RBAC Enforcement
nodes.rationale: RBAC enforced server-side. Frontend hides UI but server is the source of truth.

nodes.label: Secrets via Environment Only
nodes.rationale: Secrets via env only. Never in code, never in repo. .env is gitignored.

nodes.label: Soft-Delete Pattern
nodes.rationale: No hard deletes for business data. Use deleted_at soft-delete. Workers and audit logs are exempt.

nodes.label: 75% Test Coverage Requirement
nodes.rationale: Test coverage ≥ 75% on services. Routers and models lower; services and parsers must hit 75%+.

nodes.rationale: Frontend ships as single 725KB JS bundle with zero code-splitting. No route-based lazy loading - every page's code loads on first paint regardless of which page user is on.

nodes.label: Loading States Gap
nodes.rationale: 3 substantial pages fetch data directly with zero loading-state UI. DashboardPage (8 useQuery calls), ProjectDetailPage (2 calls), DocumentsPage (2 calls) - none reference isLoading, Skeleton, or Spinner.

nodes.label: Repository Sprawl
nodes.rationale: 59 top-level entries, 28 raw load-test CSVs at repo root, HIERARCHY.md padded with artifact filenames to pass scope-check, 39 wave folders with no live/archived distinction, 9 competing top-level orchestration docs. The engineering is real but the organization reads as sprawl.

nodes.label: Audit Trail Gap
nodes.rationale: Audit trail covers 1 of 30 services. AuditLog model exists but only time_service.py writes to it. invoice_service.py and users.py (money and RBAC-sensitive paths) write nothing.

nodes.label: Auth Assertion Bug (403 vs 401)
nodes.rationale: 5 tests assert 401 when FastAPI's HTTPBearer returns 403 for missing Authorization header. The production behaviour is correct - tests should assert 403, not 401. These are real deterministic failures, not environmental.

nodes.label: Environment-Coupled Tests
nodes.rationale: Evaluator who clones repo and runs pytest sees 2 failures. Both are environmental (Redis down), not defects - /readyz correctly reports 503 when Redis is down. But reader can't tell from output. No skip guard exists currently.

nodes.label: Frontend Regression
nodes.rationale: 3 frontend test failures caused by Excel parity commits that modified ClientForm.tsx and TimeEntryForm.tsx but never updated corresponding tests. Tests: ClientForm submit, TimeEntryForm hours validation, TimeEntryForm description requirement.

nodes.label: Job IDOR Vulnerability
nodes.rationale: Any authenticated PM-or-above who guesses or observes a job_id can read status of and download another user's exported file. Exports can contain client lists, invoices, and time data. jobs.py authorizes by role only, never by ownership, and current_user is bound but never used.

nodes.label: Service Layer Logging Gap
nodes.rationale: Zero business-logic logging across all 30 services. Middleware logs HTTP-level request/response with request_id, but nothing inside service functions logs anything. When request fails, only trace is request_end status_code=500 - no indication of which business rule tripped.

nodes.label: Orphaned Rows Bug
nodes.rationale: get_db() has no rollback() on exception and no single commit-per-request. 21 of 25 repository files call db.commit() independently. In convert_inquiry(), if step 2 or 3 raises, step 1's client row is already permanently committed - creating orphan with no automatic rollback.

nodes.label: Rate Limiting Gap
nodes.rationale: Rate limiting covers only /auth/login. All 26 other routers are unprotected including file upload (Excel import), PDF/report generation, and BOQ parsing - the expensive endpoints most worth throttling.

nodes.label: Requirements Misread Discovery
nodes.rationale: The original build produced a generic CRM, but re-reading raw meeting transcripts revealed the client's actual requested workflow was a specific ID chain (Inquiry → Client → Agreement → Token → Document Reference) that hadn't been built at all. Catching and correcting this is a stronger engineering signal than pretending it went smoothly.

nodes.label: Stale Derived Docs Problem
nodes.rationale: Waves 48-50 change real behavior: transaction semantics, rate limiting, audit-log coverage, logging, auth on /metrics, job ownership, skip markers, frontend bundle splitting. Every one invalidates a number or claim in front-door docs. Wave-47 seal was honest when made but won't be honest afterward unless re-measured.

nodes.label: Test Claim Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Evaluator-facing documents state test results that do not reproduce. README claims 566 passed/0 failed, but reality is 559 passed/7 failed/7 skipped. This is the highest-priority issue because an assessor who clones the repo sees failures against a README promising zero.

nodes.label: Unauthenticated /metrics Endpoint
nodes.rationale: /metrics is unauthenticated. Wave-37 justification (VPN/internal deploy) is reasonable as deployment assumption, but deployment is external and unconfirmed. Shipping submission that assumes network perimeter nobody verified is exactly the kind of unstated assumption evaluator will flag.

nodes.label: Backend Coverage Gaps
nodes.rationale: Overall 82% coverage but with dangerous holes in client-facing modules: pdf_service (17%), quote_service (21%), import_service (65%). These modules generate client output and handle real data migration.

nodes.label: Fake CI Gates (|| true pattern)
nodes.rationale: CI gates with || true or continue-on-error cannot fail, making green badges meaningless. This was found via grep showing 11 hits across ci.yml, security.yml, and test.yml.

nodes.rationale: Every client-facing document states the system supports 100+ concurrent users, but this comes from IT's statement about the server's capacity, not an application measurement. It has never been load-tested.

nodes.label: Content Security Policy Gap
nodes.rationale: No Content-Security-Policy header anywhere. Access + refresh tokens stored in localStorage - without CSP, any XSS becomes full token theft with no mitigation.

nodes.label: Refresh Token Rotation Gap
nodes.rationale: Refresh tokens never rotate. refresh_access_token() issues new access token but reuses SAME refresh token indefinitely. Combined with CSP gap, single XSS yields refresh token valid for full JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS with no rotation to limit blast radius.
